text:
Rowan Kim: Heads-up: onboarding friction report — users run `redwood login` (CLI writes ~/.redwood/token) then start node sample and get 401s because node only checks REDWOOD_API_KEY.

Theo Park: Seen this. Support ticket this morning. Node SDK stricter than python/cli. First impression pain.

Anya Iqbal: Proposal: agree a single precedence across SDKs/CLI: (1) REDWOOD_API_KEY env, (2) REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN env (service-scoped), (3) REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE path (default ~/.redwood/token), (4) OS keychain. Keep REDWOOD_ORG/REDWOOD_PROJECT for routing only.

Marco Silva: +1. UX items: sample apps should log the credential source on startup, CLI adds `redwood whoami` emitting JSON {org, project, credential_source}, and SDKs emit an `auth:fallback` event when falling back to file (opt-in telemetry).

Rowan Kim: Rotation behavior: gateway should return 401 with header `x-rw-auth-status: expired|invalid`. SDK logic: on expired -> try next source once, emit `auth:expired` event and surface a clear `no-valid-credentials` error with hint to `redwood login`; on invalid -> fail fast.

Theo Park: Implementation plan for node: small CredentialProvider chain (env -> service env -> file -> keychain) with overridable order, a `refreshOn401` flag, and an event hook. Tests: unit precedence + integration simulating `x-rw-auth-status: expired`.

Anya Iqbal: I'll write a short spec doc and update quickstart copy: "If you ran `redwood login`, samples will pick up CLI credentials; if you prefer env, export REDWOOD_API_KEY. Use `redwood whoami` to inspect."

devx-bot: Created issue RDW-9001: "Credential precedence parity + whoami + auth header semantics" (assigned to @Marco Silva).

Marco Silva: Taking RDW-9001. I'll open a PR for node loader + sample changes this week and follow-up on python. Thanks all.
